newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK OPPOSITION CONSERVATIVES SEIZE NARROW LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GREEK OPPOSITION CONSERVATIVES SEIZE NARROW LEAD.

text.p: Greece's opposition conservative party has a thin lead over the ruling socialists just two weeks ahead of national elections, the first major opinion poll showed on Sunday.

The conservatives, led by Miltiades Evert, were backed by 31 percent of those questioned and the ruling socialists, led by Prime Minister Costas Simitis, had 30.6 percent, the nationwide opinion poll by the private MRB group showed.

Political commentators said under Greece's voting law, which favours the first party, the conservatives would probably be able to form a single-party government with such a result in the September 22 national election.

Simitis, who called the election a year early, was hurt by the strong showing of three left-wing parties. The DIKKI party, formed by a breakaway socialist group last year, was backed by six percent of those questionned.

The Coalition of the Left had 4.2 percent and the Communist Party 4.9 percent. In contract, the Political Spring party, which broke away from the conservatives several years ago, had just three percent, the minimum national vote to win a seat in parliament.
